story.head: Panarin’s favorite opponent
paras: The Kings won the teams’ first meeting this season, 5-3 in Anaheim last night. The Kings have won two in a row, while the Ducks are 12-14-1. This is a Pacific Division matchup, with the Ducks fifth (tied for 22nd in the NHL) and the Kings seventh (29th). The Pacific has been the weakest of the four divisions so far.

The Ducks have played better than their record (.463) says: their chances are worth about .525, and losses in one-goal games have held them back. So have the Kings (.435 on chances worth .593), where their finishing has held them back.
This season, the Kings have been outscored 74-64, but only 41-38 at 5-on-5. On special teams, opponents have outscored them 22-17.

The Ducks give up a lot of dangerous shots (31st) and have had shaky goaltending (29th). The Kings, by contrast, keep dangerous shots away (1st). Anaheim has allowed 3.70 goals a game, the fourth most in the league. On the other side, the Kings leave the shooting to their forwards (lowest) and take a lot of low-quality shots (28th). The Ducks are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Kings. On top of that, both teams like to hit, especially the Ducks (4th), so expect plenty of it.

Cutter Gauthier (23 G / 9 A / 32 P in 26 GP) leads the Ducks in scoring, and Mikael Granlund (8 G / 23 A / 31 P in 26 GP) isn’t far behind. The Kings’ scoring runs through Artemi Panarin (8 G / 13 A / 21 P in 19 GP), who has a point in seven straight games against Anaheim. Adrian Kempe (7 G / 8 A / 15 P in 22 GP) isn’t far behind.

Anton Forsberg (0-7-1 / .901 SV% in 8 GS) will likely start for Los Angeles. Anaheim has two options in net: Laurent Brossoit (5-2-0 / .876 SV% in 7 GS) and Lukáš Dostál (4-7-1 / .857 SV% in 13 GS). Brossoit has started four of their last ten games, including the last one last night. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
